We do not believe that freedom can be fought for; that's why we don't want your votes. However, we need your signature on the petition to establish a political party.
Why do we start a political party if we don't want to be elected and refuse any political office? Because we want to run for office and, as part of that, open a public debate. For us, the elections represent an opportunity to get our ideas to the people - on the one hand, a link to the Urza.cz page on the ballot paper in each mailbox, but also the opportunity to participate in some pre-election debates and explain in them why we do not want to join politics.
Since the state is forcing elections on us, on the basis of which rulers we do not want (none of them), we would like to use them non-violently to spread freedom.
At the same time, we pledge to refuse any political office that we might hope to win in an election (which is extremely unlikely anyway, since we are not vying for anyone's votes).

Does it make sense to store value in Bitcoin? How can we be sure that we will not lose our savings? Nowhere at all; we never have such certainty, because it simply does not exist. While cryptocurrencies are the money of the future, they serve as better stores of value than fiat currencies; however, no one can guarantee that it will not crash unexpectedly.
However, who can guarantee such a thing with fiat? Also no one; however, it is surprising how certain a number of people consider them to be. At the same time, the lifespan of an average fiat currency does not even exceed the productive life of an individual; it's just hard to save for retirement in them. So where does the unfounded confidence come from? Well, where there is a lack of data, there is room for state propaganda.

Přednáška Adama Růžičky pro „Konferenci Svobodného přístavu 2020: Totalita včera, dnes a zítra“ nesla název „Potutelná tyranie sociální a důležitost svobody slova“.

Pod pojmem tyranie se nám obvykle vyjeví přestava násilného diktátu jedince či skupiny mocných, jenž utlačuje zbytek. Avšak myslitelé již dlouho upozorňují na to, že tyranie se může projevovat i v rovině sociální, a to způsoby hůře definovatelnými, ale o to více zákeřnými, neboť nejsou jasně vidět, ale mají na život jedinců mnohdy srovnatelný vliv jako vlády despotů. Toto ohrožení svobodných společností popsal John Stuart Mill ve své slavné eseji O svobodě a dotkl se jí i Václav Havel v Moci bezmocných, když hovořil o společenské „samo-totalitě“. Přednáška uvede základní teze problematiky sociální svobody a propojí je s nedávnými výzkumy psychologie v kontextu současných výzev demokratických společností (e.g. sociální média, názorové bubliny, fenomén rozdělených společností, apod.).

Po studiu psychologie na Masarykově univerzitě odešel Adam Růžička, MSc. MRes. na University College London, kde několik let působil jako badatel v oblasti kognitivní neurovědy a zkoumal mozek se zaměřením na lidskou řeč. V současnosti působí jako ředitel Institutu H21 v Praze, který se zaměřuje na kolektivní rozhodování, volební systémy, občanskou participaci a problematiku rozdělené společnosti.

Dalším řečníkem „Konference Svobodného přístavu 2020: Totalita včera, dnes a zítra“ byl Jan Zugar se se svou přednáškou „Severní Korea – země mnohem více otevřená, než ji vnímáme“.

Neexistuje pocitově snad více uzavřená země před okolním světem jako je Korejská lidově demokratická republika. V roce 1950-53 zde proběhla válka, při které se země rozdělila na jižní a severní část díky snaze severu, který usiloval za podpory Číny a Sovětského svazu sjednotit celou zemi pod rudou vlajkou. To se nepodařilo díky intervenci vojsk OSN, a tak po tříletém konfliktu byla Korea na tyto dvě části rozdělena 38. rovnoběžkou. Zatímco Jižní Korea je rozvojovou zemí, která jde stejným směrem jako srovnatelné orientální státy, Severní Korea je uzavřená, na média okolních zemí je uvaleno informační embargo, přístup k internetu, který je navíc interní pouze pro KLDR, je zde téměř nemožný a vládne zde tvrdá diktatura komunistické strany a klanu Kimů. Do této země se dá dostat velmi výjimečně v rámci diplomatických cest nebo studijního pobytu, což se podařilo právě Janu Zugarovi.

Jan Zugar je absolvent VUT v Brně, člen Mladých křesťanských demokratů a odpůrce komunismu.
title_en: Students for Liberty: Urza and Martin Pánek on freedom of speech (not only n) and social networks
text_en:
Liberty Webinars is a series of webinars by Students for Liberty CZ and Slovak Students For Liberty, which they organize at a time when face-to-face events are not possible. This time, Martin Pánek and Urza debated on the topic of freedom of expression and social networks. 
------------------------------------------------------------------------------
The topic of the panel is freedom of speech in the context of recent events involving the suspension of a considerable number of often significantly politically exposed accounts on various social networks, and the so-called deplatforming of some public officials, such as former US President Donald Trump.

Is it an interference with freedom of speech, as many of those banned have claimed? Are social networks and platforms for the sharing of ideological content more than just a private enterprise, and therefore need to be legislated as part of the public power to limit how they regulate their content? What is freedom of speech anyway, and what are its limits?

Dalším neuvěřitelně poutavým řečníkem „Konference Svobodného přístavu 2020: Totalita včera, dnes a zítra“ byla Lidija Zavoralová se svou přednáškou „Iluze svobody jako větší zlo versus totalita“.

Jak vůbec poznáme, co a kdy je totalita a kde totalita začíná? Příběh Lidije Zavoralové začíná už v jejích třinácti letech, když bojovala za shazování srbského socialistického režimu pod vládou Miloševiće. Osobně tiskla letáky a vyzývala celou školu, aby šla demonstrovat se studenty. Následně pak v 19 letech zjistila, že je v pasti, všechno bylo se svobodou jinak, než se jí zdálo, ale i přes tuto skepsi začala po roce studia v Americe pracovat pro tajné služby, dodávala jim informace a znovu myslela, že bojuje pro demokracii svého státu. V přednášce bude povídat i o tom, jaké konkrétní úkoly v rámci této své osobní mise dostávala.

Lidija Zavoralová je freedom-hacker, byznys konzultantka a spisovatelka dětských knížek.

Speciálním hostem „Konference Svobodného přístavu 2020: Totalita včera, dnes a zítra“ byl řečník, Richard Vokoun s přednáškou „Diktatura versus totalita, surveillance - a kde je svoboda?“.

Každý historik vám popíše, jak fungovaly historické totality. Jak ale rozpoznat budoucí totalitní ideologie a jak je přežít? Jaký je zásadní rozdíl mezi totalitou a diktaturou? Může totalita vzniknout pouze skrze stát, nebo se reálně vyskytují i "grasroots" totality od tajných skupinek fanatiků?
Ve studiu totalit si postupně prošel od historického přes systémové, politologické, sociologické a psychologické hledisko a výsledkem je syntéza univerzálně platných principů fungování totalit.

Richard Vokoun 15 let studuje totalitní režimy a ideologie, které za nimi stojí. Jeho profesí je analýza technických systémů a předvídání jejich rizik a selhání, ale tyto dovednosti používá i k připomínkování zákonů. V práci vidí „pod pokličku“ šmírovacích a dohledových systémů. Má i průřezové znalosti z bezpečnostních studií, historie a fungování tajných služeb a represivních orgánů, křesťanské a islámské teologie.

Druhým přednášejícím „Konference Svobodného přístavu 2020: Totalita včera, dnes a zítra“ byl Urza se svou přednáškou „Různé tváře zla aneb Rozpoznejte totalitu“.

Ač se snad všichni shodnou na tom, že nechtějí žít v totalitě, z nějakého důvodu jsou totalitní režimy neodmyslitelnou součástí naší historie; a to nejen dávno minulé, ale také celkem nedávné, zkrátka neustále přicházejí znovu a znovu. Ptáte se, jak je to možné, když téměř všichni totalitu odmítají? Inu, málokdo ji totiž nabídne lidem přímo; totalitní režimy typicky přicházejí pod rouškou slibů bezpečí, prosperity, blahobytu, a často dokonce i svobody. Historie bohužel ukazuje, že většina lidí totalitu nerozezná, dokud není příliš pozdě. A protože si nechce (snad nejen) Urza tuto historii zopakovat, během této přednášky se pokusí vás naučit rozpoznávat příchody totalitních režimů, dokud je ještě čas.

Urza je anarchokapitalistický autor; napsal asi tisíc libertariánských textů na web i do tištěných médií a první českou knihu o anarchokapitalismu. O svobodě, etice, volném trhu, ekonomii a roli státu ve společnosti nejen přes deset let čte, přemýšlí a píše, ale též přednáší, natáčí videa a je zván do různých pořadů i panelových diskusí. Spolu s manželkou Terezou tvoří Svobodný přístav; vede český a slovenský Institut Ludwiga von Misese, jehož je spoluzakladatelem; patří do předsednictva spolku Svoboda učení a aktivně spolupracuje s mnoha libertariánskými iniciativami. title_cs: Debata pro loutky v divadle DISK
text_cs:
Divadlo DISK pořádá cyklus diskusí „Debaty pro loutky“. Toto je záznam z prvního pilotního zkušebního dílu; na celém formátu se neustále pracuje, takže budoucí debaty mohou vypadat jinak.
Smyslem diskuse bylo, že každý účastník byl zastoupen loutkou coby avatarem a neznal identitu ostatních. Prošel jsem spoustou debat; je to součást mé práce. Tato se od všech ostatních odlišovala asi nejvíce; byla to příjemná změna. Už na první pohled se mi ten nápad líbil, ale až během diskuse jsem jej plně docenil – člověk se může daleko lépe soustředit na téma samotné a není ničím rozptylován.
Po první části, z níž pochází záznam, následovala ještě druhá – s odkrytými tvářemi; její záznam mi bohužel divadlo neposkytlo. Každopádně jsem byl překvapen, že mě řada lidí z publika poznala (nejlepší byl komentář: „Snad každý pozná anarchokapitalistu, když ho slyší.“ – něco takového by před několika lety určitě nezaznělo); a debata loutek patrně splnila účel i v tom smyslu, že mi jedna z posluchaček řekla, že mě poprvé doopravdy poslouchala, aniž to předem odsoudila na základě toho, kdo jsem (a prý jí to, co jsem říkal, dávalo smysl).

– Urza (www.urza.cz); autor knihy Anarchokapitalismus; tvůrce Svobodného přístavu; spoluzakladatel a hlava Institutu Ludwiga von Misese; člen předsednictva Svobody učení

What exactly is anarcho-capitalism? The longer I try to present it to individuals and to an increasingly wider public, the more I recognize that it is not very difficult to describe it in a few hours; the more interesting challenge is to summarize the main idea in half an hour, which I just tried. For seasoned libertarians, it will not be anything new in terms of information, although I believe that even you can take something away from the way of presentation; for others, it is one of the theoretical videos, the purpose of which is to put the individual topics that we discuss with interesting guests into some kind of coherent framework. title_en: About marginal utility with Petr Hála
text_en:
One of the regular listeners – Petr Firefanatic Hála – disagreed with my concept of marginal utility theory on one of the streams; he did what I hope others of you will follow: He debated me on the record on the subject; and it gave rise to an interesting debate about the economy, which can hopefully bring something to others as well. We discussed the value of one thousand crowns for billionaires and for the homeless. Can we increase "aggregate utility" by giving a billionaire's thousand to a homeless person? I will be happy for your comments and opinions in the comments; and if you are interested in discussing any topic with me in this way, please contact me, I am certainly open to it.

– Petr Firefanatic Hall; anarcho-capitalist; supporter of the Free Port; math physicist; programmer
– Urza (www.urza.cz); author of Anarchocapitalism; creator of Freeport; co-founder and head of the Ludwig von Mises Institute; member of the Freedom of Learning board

text_cs:
Každý člověk si od malinka vědomě i nevědomě vytváří různá pouta nejrůznějších druhů s okolím; zabránit něčemu takovému nelze, nejspíše by to ani nebylo žádoucí. Obecně pak máme za to, že každý by měl mít časem svobodu o vazbách ve svém životě rozhodovat. Málokomu jsou po chuti organizace či sekty, které se snaží vytvářet silné emoční vazby v malých dětech, aby jim byly oddané dřív, než budou schopny efektivního kritického myšlení. Kdo byl však sám takto indoktrinován, ten typicky na podobném jednání neshledává nic závadného; naopak má nezřídka sám tendenci v dobré víře činit dalším generacím totéž.

– Urza (www.urza.cz); autor knihy Anarchokapitalismus; tvůrce Svobodného přístavu; spoluzakladatel a hlava Institutu Ludwiga von Misese; člen předsednictva Svobody učení

Although many people already understand why socialism and central planning in general do not work, there is a belief in society that certain industries must be centrally planned by the state because "it cannot be done otherwise"; and healthcare is unfortunately one of them. People are afraid that under capitalist health care, "the poor would die in the streets", which they are trying to fix with socialist health care; in that, unfortunately, people die as a result of misallocation of resources, but it's not seen as much because no one says to anyone, "We're not providing care." But it happens in practice, or the care provided is completely inadequate; as a result, of course, a lot of people die, although it is impossible to measure exactly how many there are, but sometimes specific cases can be pointed to.
As a doctor, Tereza has first-hand access to that system; in this livestream you can ask her anything you can think of on the topic. You can also call our Studio via Skype!

The interview with the politician and former finance minister Vlastimil Tlustý took place in a surprisingly friendly spirit; most of the time we discussed the functioning of the state, its expansiveness and parasitism on its own citizens. The corona crisis is ongoing; and we can see many of its manifestations - lack of personnel, lack of protective equipment, lack of capacity... Which of the things we know have manifested themselves in exactly this way in the past? Practically anything in socialist/communist central planning; and therefore I cannot, with the best of my will, attribute the exact same manifestations of problems in our socialist healthcare system to coincidence. The free market is simply efficient in allocating resources; central planning is not. Everything that the theories of the Austrian school of economics tell us is confirmed by the practice of our lives; will we finally start listening to the Austrian economists, or will we close our eyes to them like previous generations?

– Urza (www.urza.cz); author of Anarchocapitalism; creator of Freeport; co-founder and head of the Ludwig von Mises Institute; member of the Freedom of Learning board

The police have adopted a strategy of honking at level crossings, where they look for a driver to cross the crossing after the shutters are up, but before the red warning lights go out; at some crossings, the barriers go up a little before the red light stops. Whenever I criticize this police practice, someone comes up who starts to stand up for them and defend them by saying that the barriers can go down again right after they are raised, because the red light doesn't have to stop shining at all, if another train goes by for a while. Why do I consider this argument fundamentally wrong, even though I agree that something like this can happen? You will learn this and other connections in the video!

Jaká je pravděpodobnost, že člověk způsobuje klimatickou změnu? Lze něco takového spočítat? Pokud ano, jak?

The former Slovenian ambassador in Prague collects evidence of corruption at the Czech embassy in Morocco; in his opinion, there is shopping with visas. He submitted the recordings to the Police of the Czech Republic; she thanked him, but apparently she has been out of action for many months. Damjan Prelovšek does not give up and hopes that if he makes the case public, he will perhaps make the police act. Although we know nothing about the case, and as anarchists we are certainly not law enforcement, we decided to give him space; on the one hand, because he seems to believe in his stuff, he played us the recordings (according to which it really seems that visas are being traded), but above all, to show people in practice those features of the state that we constantly describe on a theoretical level.

Although most people imagine something under the term "monopoly" - and even suspect that it is something harmful; however, few distinguish between a true monopoly and a dominant market player, but what's worse - the biggest, most harmful, most violent and most widespread monopoly is completely neglected and ignored. Yes, this is a state that can afford everything that no one else could afford. How is that? Well, by consistently abusing its monopoly position in education, it constantly indoctrinates everyone with its propaganda from the earliest age; people are then willing to view the state in a completely different way than all other subjects.
Through the analysis of the monopoly position of the state, the attitudes of anarcho-capitalists can also be clearly described. Contrary to popular belief, they do not want a world without the services that states provide; in fact, they only seek to de-monopolize the state and enable competition.

Intellectual property represents one of many areas of friction between statists and libertarians; however, the truth is that while most people defend intellectual property, its detractors can be found in both camps. Even among the greats of the Austrian school of economics, we have its supporters from the past (Ludwig von Mises, Murray Newton Rothbard), although nowadays more of them take the opposite position (Norman Stephan Kinsella, Walter Block, Jeffrey Tucker). When I lecture on intellectual property, I usually oppose the proponents of centric law; however, today Dominik Hrubý - a supporter of decentralized society - defended intellectual property against my arguments.

title_en: Urza with Bratříček on freedom of speech
text_en:
After almost a year, we met YouTuber Bratříček again; last year we had a debate about anarcho-capitalism in general (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=RT-BYX_VmP8&list=PLmwDL0lIJTxBIIAJ8m7j32KYTqP09n-xL), this year we focused mainly on freedom of speech and "censorship" carried out by large internet corporations. The debate loosely follows on from my discussion with Daniel Vávra (Bratříček holds very similar views). What do you think? And what will next year bring us?

– Little brother; youtuber; businessman
– Urza (www.urza.cz); author of Anarchocapitalism; creator of Freeport; co-founder and head of the Ludwig von Mises Institute; member of the Freedom of Learning board

text_cs:
S velkou radostí jsme přijali již třetí pozvání na letní Misesovu akademii Liberálního institutu. Krom přednášky o anarchokapitalismu jsme se všemi účastníky ještě rozebírali kapitolu Nečestný policajt z knihy Obhajoba neobhajitelného od Waltera Blocka, jehož považuji za jednoho z nejlogičtějších anarchokapitalistů.
Z debaty není obraz, pouze zvuk, jehož kvalita je navíc neslavná, za což se omlouvám, ale vyčistil jsem ho, jak se dalo.

– Tereza Urzová; tvůrce Svobodného přístavu; hlava Institutu Ludwiga von Misese; vydavatelka knihy Anarchokapitalismus; členka Students for Liberty

I've been reading D-FENS's weblog since I was fifteen; it was one of the first places I published, where I learned to write, debate, and think critically. What if someone had a child dying in anarcho-capitalism that would require 50 million to save, which they didn't have? What then? How would the market deal with this!? Well, the state probably wouldn't ask for another 5 million in protection money (called VAT) from the money that people voluntarily collected. And what if someone was dying in capitalist healthcare because there was no money to treat them? Well, in that case at least he would know and maybe have a chance to try to do something about it; it happens all the time in socialist healthcare, it's just not talked about and no one calls the cases that way. And what is the price of human life? Can something like this be converted into money at all? Don't anarcho-capitalists do something like that? Well... SÚKL definitely does.

There are a number of barriers and pitfalls in communication with socialists and generally everyone from the opposite side of the opinion spectrum; however, many of them are more communicative in nature than fundamental. How we perceive the world is, of course, based on who we are as people; and the way we think and communicate is based on the kind of people we are. So it is not surprising that an individualist will understand the words of another individualist better than the words of a collectivist; even if both were trying to communicate exactly the same content. Let's try together to understand our differences and weaken the communication barriers a little!

There is a widespread belief among the general public that ID cards are needed; it simply wouldn't be possible without them. But why exactly? There aren't many good reasons; actually there is none. Behavioral economics comes with an interesting critique of the concept of homo economicus and the concept of bounded rationality; it also disrupts some of the models used by mainstream economics by showing the "irrational" behavior of people. At first glance, it seems to be the antithesis of the Austrian economy (and many people perceive it as such); however, I personally think that these two economic schools have more in common than it might seem at first glance (although their starting points and conclusions are undoubtedly different). At the end, we will also recall how the Austrians perceive rationality; and why it is not a completely happy definition from my point of view.

The four types of market failures (imperfect competition, information asymmetry, public goods and externalities) are taught in every possible economic school, constantly repeated and taken more or less as a given; unfortunately, they are not discussed much anymore, and in addition, many people do not even think about them much, they simply learn them for the test and continue to take them as fact. I certainly do not want to contradict what economists are so fond of proving, namely that market allocation is not Pareto-optimal; however, I would like to discuss what it even means and what consequences can be derived from it (and especially point out what consequences cannot be derived from it, although unfortunately this often happens). And does it even make sense to call something like this a market failure?

Daniel Vávra made an interesting video about freedom of speech (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OQ1eBSZvFSo); and since you sent it to me massively and asked for opinions, I decided to respond in the form of a video of my own. I've tried to frame it so that it makes sense even if you choose not to look at what I'm responding to. I deal with the issue of communication platforms operated by large corporations and their censorship, which is (at least partially) pushed by states. I try to distinguish between personal preferences regarding free expression and look for a line between subjective beliefs on how to set rules and (not) imposing them on others; it is no less important to distinguish between a (state-enforced) monopoly and a (more or less market-based) dominant player (with existing competition; even if it is significantly weaker at the given moment).

Network security is an increasingly important topic in the age of sophistication of the Internet; and recently VPNs have come into vogue. That in itself is great because people want to be anonymous and protect their digital freedom. Unfortunately, however, they often use technologies that they have no idea how they work; it can backfire on them. And since I've been getting a lot of questions about VPN lately, I decided to make a video; maybe I will help someone from unwanted exposure of their sensitive data and personal data. At the end of the video, I discuss some general principles of network security.

The media was flashed with unsalted unsalted news that the government is amending the law so that the CNB can buy government bonds. Although minimal space has been devoted to this topic, it is probably the most dangerous thing that the current government has demonstrated during the crisis; quite possibly without most of its representatives realizing it. And since the general public doesn't know much about it, we decided to explain from the ground up what the problem is; we will start with the history of money, we will also deal with fractional banking, we will also get to the harmfulness of artificial inflation, the threat of apocalyptic hyperinflation, and we will end with the connection with the actions of the government and the CNB.
--------
You can find a counter-argument to the postponing consumption claim (as well as a description of the emergence of business cycles) here:

The coronavirus is not only dangerous as a disease, but also as a social phenomenon; and few governments miss an opportunity to use the population's fear to their advantage - for the gradual introduction of totality. Our government has already begun; and I have no illusions that she would just let herself be stopped. Babiš will be the "savior of the people" and everyone will have to keep their mouths shut.
For example, have you noticed the amendment to the law on military intelligence, which gives the secret services the ability to monitor all network communication on the Czech Internet? Or did it fit in with the news about the coronavirus?

text_en:

Why do deputies and senators have immunity? What is this institute for? At first glance, the reason sounds quite reasonable; but upon closer examination it is a complete mockery.
How are restraining orders related to parliamentary immunity? Not directly; but there is a certain parallel between these two exceptions to the (bad) law. Preservation orders are actually parliamentary immunity "in reverse".

Another anarcho-communist accepted my invitation to the Freeport Studio. We had a very interesting debate, which I consider an important part of my effort to conduct a dialogue with anarchists from other anarchist schools, which is not so easy, as anarcho-communists typically refuse to discuss with anarcho-capitalists (at least in the Czech Republic). The last speaker of the "Free Harbor Conference 2020: Totality yesterday, today and tomorrow" was Palo Lupták with his lecture "Opt-out from the system: How to achieve economic and personal freedom by using globality and flexibility".

1. Choose a suitable country for your permanent residency.
2. Choose a suitable country as the headquarters for your company.
3. Remove centers of interest in your home country.
4. Cancel your bank account.
5. Transfer your finances to cryptocurrencies, prefer truly anonymous ones, support cryptocurrency friendly services.
6. Choose international health insurance.
7. Choose your international mobile operator.
8. Support the sharing economy.
9. Help your friends opt-out of the system.

Palo Lupták is a crypto-anarchist and volunteer focused on technology and hacking society. He is the founder of hacking companies in the field of IT security (Nethemba, Hacktrophy) and contemporary art (Satori). He co-founded the Bratislava and Prague hackerspaces (Progressbar and Paralelni Polis).

Adam Růžička's lecture for the "Free Harbor Conference 2020: Totality yesterday, today and tomorrow" was entitled "Creeping social tyranny and the importance of freedom of speech".

Under the term tyranny, we usually imagine the violent dictate of a powerful individual or group that oppresses the rest. However, thinkers have long pointed out that tyranny can also manifest itself on a social level, in ways that are harder to define, but all the more insidious, because they are not clearly visible, but often have a comparable influence on the lives of individuals as despotic governments. This threat to free societies was described by John Stuart Mill in his famous essay On Freedom, and Václav Havel also touched on it in The Power of the Powerless when he spoke of social "self-totality". The lecture will present the basic theses of the issue of social freedom and connect them with recent psychological research in the context of the current challenges of democratic societies (e.g. social media, opinion bubbles, the phenomenon of divided societies, etc.).

After studying psychology at Masaryk University, Adam Růžička, MSc. MRes. at University College London, where he worked for several years as a researcher in the field of cognitive neuroscience and researched the brain with a focus on human speech. He currently works as the director of the H21 Institute in Prague, which focuses on collective decision-making, electoral systems, civic participation and the issue of a divided society.

The next speaker at the "Freeport Conference 2020: Totality yesterday, today and tomorrow" was Jan Zugar with his lecture "North Korea - a country much more open than we perceive it".

There is perhaps no country more emotionally closed to the outside world than the Democratic People's Republic of Korea. In 1950-53, a war took place here, during which the country was divided into southern and northern parts due to the efforts of the north, which sought, with the support of China and the Soviet Union, to unite the entire country under the red flag. This failed thanks to the intervention of UN troops, and so after a three-year conflict, Korea was divided into these two parts by the 38th parallel. While South Korea is a developing country that is moving in the same direction as comparable eastern states, North Korea is closed, an information embargo is imposed on the media of the surrounding countries, access to the Internet, which is also internal only to the DPRK, is almost impossible and the harsh dictatorship of the Communist Party and the Kim clan rules here. It is very rare to get to this country as part of diplomatic trips or a study stay, which Jan Zugar was able to do.

Jan Zugar is a graduate of BUT in Brno, a member of the Young Christian Democrats and an opponent of communism.

Another incredibly engaging speaker at the "2020 Freeport Conference: Totality yesterday, today and tomorrow" was Lidija Zavoralová with her lecture "The illusion of freedom as a greater evil versus totality".

How do we even know what and when totality is and where totality begins? Lidija Zavoralová's story begins at the age of thirteen, when she fought for the overthrow of the Serbian socialist regime under Milošević's rule. She personally printed leaflets and called on the whole school to go and demonstrate with the students. Subsequently, at the age of 19, she discovered that she was trapped, everything about freedom was different than she had imagined, but despite this skepticism, after a year of studying in America, she started working for the secret services, supplying them with information and once again thinking that she was fighting for the democracy of her country. In the lecture, she will also talk about what specific tasks she received as part of this personal mission.

Lidija Zavoralová is a freedom-hacker, business consultant and writer of children's books.

The special guest of the "Free Harbor Conference 2020: Totality yesterday, today and tomorrow" was the speaker, Richard Vokoun, with the lecture "Dictatorship versus totality, surveillance - and where is freedom?".

Any historian will tell you how historical totalities worked. But how to recognize future totalitarian ideologies and how to survive them? What is the fundamental difference between totalitarianism and dictatorship? Can totality arise only through the state, or are there real "grassroots" totalities from secret groups of fanatics?
In the study of totalitarianism, he gradually went from the historical to the systemic, political, sociological and psychological point of view, and the result is a synthesis of universally applicable principles of functioning of totalitarianism.

Richard Vokoun has been studying totalitarian regimes and the ideologies behind them for 15 years. His profession is analyzing technical systems and predicting their risks and failures, but he also uses these skills to comment on laws. He sees "under the hood" of spying and surveillance systems at work. He also has interdisciplinary knowledge of security studies, the history and functioning of secret services and repressive bodies, Christian and Islamic theology.

The second speaker of the "2020 Freeport Conference: Totality Yesterday, Today and Tomorrow" was Urza with his lecture "The Different Faces of Evil or Recognize Totality".

Although everyone can probably agree that they don't want to live in totalitarianism, for some reason totalitarian regimes are an inherent part of our history; and not only long past, but also quite recent, in short, they keep coming again and again. How is this possible, you ask, when almost everyone rejects totalitarianism? Well, few people offer it to people directly; totalitarian regimes typically come under the guise of promises of safety, prosperity, well-being, and often even freedom. Unfortunately, history shows that most people do not recognize totalitarianism until it is too late. And because Urza does not want (perhaps not only) to repeat this history, during this lecture he will try to teach you to recognize the arrival of totalitarian regimes while there is still time.

Urza is an anarcho-capitalist author; wrote about a thousand libertarian texts on the web and in print media and the first Czech book on anarcho-capitalism. For more than ten years, he not only reads, thinks and writes about freedom, ethics, the free market, the economy and the role of the state in society, but also lectures, makes videos and is invited to various programs and panel discussions. Together with his wife Teresa, he forms the Free Harbor; he heads the Czech and Slovak Institute of Ludwig von Mises, of which he is a co-founder; belongs to the board of the Freedom of Learning association and actively cooperates with many libertarian initiatives. You can find more about him on the Urza.cz website.

title_en: Debate for puppets in the DISK theater
text_en:
The DISK Theater organizes a cycle of discussions "Debates for Puppets". This is footage from the first pilot test piece; the entire format is a constant work in progress, so future debates may look different.
The point of the discussion was that each participant was represented by a puppet as an avatar and did not know the identity of the others. I've been through a lot of debates; it's part of my job. This one was probably the most different from all the others; it was a nice change. I liked the idea at first glance, but only during the discussion did I fully appreciate it - one can focus much better on the topic itself and is not distracted by anything.
After the first part, from which the recording comes, there was a second one - with exposed faces; Unfortunately, the theater did not provide me with her recording. Anyway, I was surprised that a number of people in the audience recognized me (the best comment was: "I hope everyone knows an anarcho-capitalist when they hear one." - something that certainly wouldn't have been heard a few years ago); and the puppet debate probably served its purpose also in the sense that one of the listeners told me that for the first time she really listened to me without pre-judging me based on who I was (and she said what I was saying made sense to her).

– Urza (www.urza.cz); author of Anarchocapitalism; creator of Freeport; co-founder and head of the Ludwig von Mises Institute; member of the Freedom of Learning board

In the Ostrava hospital, a man armed with an illegal weapon shot six people and injured two others; he finally ran away. The police caught up with him within a few hours, after which the person in question shot himself.
How would it turn out if someone else was armed in that waiting room? Gun bans make it impossible for those who respect them to defend themselves against people who ignore them. What are the advantages and disadvantages of an armed society?

title_en: Symposion 2019 at the Jan Kepler Gymnasium
text_en:
From an early age, each person consciously and unconsciously creates various bonds of various kinds with the environment; it is impossible to prevent something like that, it would probably not even be desirable. In general, we believe that everyone should have the freedom to make decisions about the ties in their life over time. Few people like organizations or sects that try to create strong emotional bonds in young children to be devoted to them before they are capable of effective critical thinking. However, those who themselves have been indoctrinated in this way typically do not find anything objectionable in such behavior; on the contrary, he himself often tends in good faith to do the same to other generations.

I would like to shorten my talk, increase the space for discussion and deformalize everything a bit; moreover, I probably won't be the only one lecturing.
At the lecture, we will talk about science and research in a free market environment. How and by whom could science be funded? Would basic research develop somehow, or only applied? The Industrial Revolution is often referred to as a period of savage capitalism in which people worked in bleak conditions, often at a very young age; that's kind of true, but not entirely true - it was thanks to the industrial revolution that child labor came to an end.
Another topic we address is automation and the phenomenon of machines taking people's jobs. This is a phenomenon that takes place not tens, not hundreds, but even thousands of years. Nevertheless, our society continues to grow rich and prosperous. How is that possible?

– Tereza Urzová; creator of Freeport; head of the Ludwig von Mises Institute; publisher of the book Anarchocapitalismus; member of Students for Liberty

Tématem přednášky i diskuse budou lidská práva v anarchokapitalismu. Jak k nim anarchokapitalisté přistupují, když jsou jim svatá jen práva vlastnická? Chrání princip neagrese (NAP) lidská práva? Doing a Nazi salute on a school trip to a concentration camp doesn't pay; in Poland it is punishable by up to three years in prison. Most people would probably agree that this is a pretty stupid idea; but where is the limit of free speech?
Property rights in a free market free society give relatively clear answers to this and other questions; nevertheless, certain ambiguities may arise in specific cases, which we discuss in the Free Port Studio.

In the seventeenth episode of Freeport Studios, we finally had our first guest; he was minarchist Roman Kříž, founder of the Libertarian Institute and member of the Free Citizens Party. His approach to the spread of libertarian ideas is diametrically different from mine, but this does not stand in the way of mutual respect, because we both strive for the same thing.
As this is the first episode with a guest, I would appreciate it if you could comment on whether you think this format is better or worse than when we talk only with Terezka.

Anarchokapitalisté používají logiku, kolektivističtí anarchisté spíše cit; dříve bych řekl, že logika je prostě lepší, dnes už to prostě nevím. – Urza (www.urza.cz); autor knihy Anarchokapitalismus; tvůrce Svobodného přístavu; spoluzakladatel a hlava Institutu Ludwiga von Misese; člen předsednictva Svobody učení
text_en:
We know the term "probability" from mathematics and everyday life; at this level we can intuitively work with it. However, the problem arises when these planes begin to intersect; then mere conjectures and opinions can become proofs and facts in the eyes of others.
What is the probability that humans are causing climate change? Can such a thing be calculated? If so, how?

– Urza (www.urza.cz); author of Anarchocapitalism; creator of Freeport; co-founder and head of the Ludwig von Mises Institute; member of the Freedom of Learning board

text_cs:

Zajímavé je, že oni sami vidí, že stát tady selhává, ale místo aby to akceptovali, volají právě po státním řešení. Etatismus je všudypřítomný a bohužel zasahuje i skeptiky; a do jisté míry vlastně i anarchisty.

– Tereza Urzová; tvůrce Svobodného přístavu; hlava Institutu Ludwiga von Misese; členka Students for Liberty

Catalan separatists received heavy penalties for holding a referendum on Catalan independence, which contradicted the Spanish constitution. But what about the right to self-determination?
What about other territories seeking secession? How are Catalonia, Tibet or Kosovo related? We will also mention Crimea. But mainly we will look at separation and the right to self-determination from an anarcho-capitalist point of view.

title_cs: Anarchokapitalismus, díl devatenáctý: V širším kontextu…
text_cs:
Jakým způsobem dojít od obrovského všežravého státu k anarchokapitalismu? A kudy cesta rozhodně nevede? I o tom si budeme povídat na poslední regulérní přednášce tohoto cyklu. Mnozí z vás si správně všimli, že většina přednášek byla „na jedno brdo“ v tom smyslu, že se jednalo o aplikaci téhož principu na různá odvětví lidské činnosti. Tento princip bych rád objasnil a formuloval obecně; zejména pro ty, kdo jej nepostřehli. A konečně zasadíme anarchokapitalismus do nějakého kontextu ostatních anarchistických škol, kterých je celá řada a o nichž určitě ještě mnoho uslyšíte.

In the eighth volume of the Free Port Studio, we deal with the information and propaganda war between the EU and Russia; we speculate on the possibilities of further development after a possible Czexit and think about what it actually means when a state falls under someone's "sphere of influence".
How to fight misinformation? But above all, how not to fight so that it is not counterproductive? And who should pay for this fight?

Na přednášku dorazilo překvapivě hodně studentů; ačkoliv měli na výběr z mnoha přednášek, nebylo nakonec ani dost židlí, tak museli sedět na nábytku. Kladli skvělé otázky; celou debatu považuji za velice konstruktivní. Především se nakonec ukázalo, že se skoro všichni dozvěděli něco nového!

Come and talk about the free market to people who are studying social work, so they are clear enough that certain things just have to be done by the state. Potřebujeme státy, abychom nezdevastovali přírodu a životní prostředí? Bude-li naše společnost „řízena“ jen a pouze volnotržně, zanecháme našim potomkům více než jen zamořenou vodu, vzduch i půdu? Kdo by bez státu chránil ohrožené živočišné druhy? A jak bez státu prosadit trvale udržitelný rozvoj? K vysvětlování této zajímavé problematiky budu notně užívat poznatků rakouské ekonomické školy, které jsme (většinou opakovaně) rozebírali v předchozích přednáškách; vřele doporučuji si je znovu osvěžit.

Jsme však individualisté, z principu se nekádrujeme a spojuje nás mimo jiné neochota slepě poslouchat autority, takže pro každé naše „typicky“ existují výjimky. To je na jednu stranu skvělé, leč na stranu druhou v tomto konkrétním případě považuji za extrémně důležité říci k tomu pár slov…

text_cs:
Když se řekne „volnotržní zdravotnictví“, většinu lidí hned napadnou horentní částky za lékařské úkony, které si běžný smrtelník nemůže prostě dovolit platit, takže mu nezbývá než žít v nemoci; nebo dokonce umřít. Jak bychom si bez státu mohli dovolit platit za lékařskou péči? Kdo by dohlížel na kvalitu? Jak tržně překonat obrovskou informační asymetrii mezi lékařem a pacientem? Není volnotržní zdravotnictví asociální a hrůzný systém, skrze který mohou mocní ždímat bezmocné a nemocné? Odpovědi na tyto a mnohé další otázky se dozvíte, když přijdete na přednášku; a v následné diskusi pak můžete položit i vlastní dotazy.

I would like to shorten my talk, increase the space for discussion and deformalize everything a bit; moreover, I probably won't be the only one lecturing.

text_cs:
Myslíte si, že bez státu a jeho regulací by zaměstnanci neměli žádného zastání, takže by je zaměstnavatelé mohli dřít z kůže? V tom případě je tato přednáška právě pro vás! Ukážeme si, proč by volný a neregulovaný trh práce zaměstnancům nejen neuškodil, ale naopak by jejich situaci v mnoha ohledech zlepšil; stát totiž svou „ochranou“ poskytuje zaměstnancům tak trochu medvědí službou. Nahlédnout, jak přesně a proč tomu tak je, není vůbec tak složité; stačí přijít na přednášku, kde si budeme mimo jiné povídat i o dětské práci a mnoha dalších zajímavých věcech.

We will discuss an often inflected topic with anarcho-capitalism - inequality. Where does it come from? Is it possible to somehow remove her from the world? You will learn the answers to these and many other questions at this lecture!

Umírali by ve volnotržní společnosti chudí na ulicích hlady? Co by si bez státu počali staří lidé? Tyto a mnohé další otázky se chystám zodpovědět na dvanácté přednášce z cyklu Anarchokapitalismus; následně se o těchto tématech můžeme bavit v diskusi.

title_cs: HCPP17: Liberate education from the state!
text_cs:
Compulsory school attendance is not only immoral, but it also represents the initial reason of our economical lack of freedom; State education costs money, also it's a source of the state propaganda and statist indoctrination. This is the main cause of the conviction of people that free market fails in so many areas, so we need the state authority to replace it. Why don't they teach us anything about the impossibility of economic calculation in the central planning? How easily can the authority of a teacher be replaced by the state authorities? And how can we keep the freedom when we spend the most important years of our lives in the jail?
Sorry for my horrible english; it is not so good in general and moreover I felt physically quite bad this time.

Presenting: Zdeňka Staňková and Urza (www.urza.cz) of Svoboda učení (www.svobodauceni.cz).

The association of philosophers Libomudravna from Hradec Králové invited Mr. and Mrs. Urza to lecture on anarcho-capitalism; the organizer and I agreed on a very short lecture, which served rather as an introduction to the subsequent debate. The discussion was really beneficial and the questions were very interesting; after all, judge for yourself.

– Tereza Urzová; creator of Freeport; head of the Ludwig von Mises Institute; publisher of the book Anarchocapitalismus; member of Students for Liberty

title_cs: Prague Business Club: Kdo by stavěl silnice?
text_cs:
Byl jsem požádán podnikateli z Prague Business Clubu o soukromou přednášku o dopravní infrastruktuře na volném trhu; nabídce jsem s radostí vyhověl a přenášku přizpůsobil této cílové skupině, ačkoliv téma se samozřejmě do značné míry (ne zcela) překrývá s jedenáctým dílem cyklu Anarchokapitalismus z Polis.
Jste-li skeptici a praktici každodenní reality, přednáška může být na váš vkus trochu moc optimistická a „vizionářská“; v takovém případě doporučuji zhlédnout místo ní právě stejnojmennou přednášku z cyklu Anarchokapitalismus. Tak či tak se v obou případech velice liší směřování otázek v diskusi.

– Urza (www.urza.cz)

title_en: Teresa in the Reefer Madness debate

– Tereza Urzová; creator of Freeport; head of the Ludwig von Mises Institute; publisher of the book Anarchocapitalismus; member of Students for Liberty

text_cs:
Bylo mi ctí přijmout pozvání na Misesovu akademii Liberálního institutu, kde jsem měl dvě přednášky.
Toto je záznam z první z nich – o svobodném vzdělávání; publikum tvořili z drtivé většiny libertariáni, kteří o daném tématu již leccos vědí, čemuž byla přednáška přizpůsobena. Přednášku na podobné téma cílovanou na širší veřejnost naleznete v seznamu videí „Anarchokapitalismus v Polis“ pod názvem „Anarchokapitalismus, díl sedmý: Školství“.

– Urza (www.urza.cz)
title_en: Debate on anarchy at the Jan Kepler High School
text_en:
The students of Jan Kepler Gymnasium invited me to a panel discussion at Symposion 2018; the topic was supposed to be anarchy, left-wing anarchists were also invited, but they refused, so in the end I debated alone with Ilona Švihlíková. I think that it was still an interesting panel with good questions from the audience, but above all from the presenters, who confided in me before the discussion that they had never moderated anything before, but they definitely performed their roles well.

– Urza (www.urza.cz); author of Anarchocapitalism; creator of Freeport; co-founder and head of the Ludwig von Mises Institute; member of the Freedom of Learning board

text_cs:
Paralelní Polis uspořádala diskusi na téma „Týden hrdosti LGBT“; původně se tedy jmenovala jinak, ale došlo na právní výhružky kvůli ochranné známce. Zúčastnili se zastánci i odpůrci a zazněla spousta zajímavých názorů; jejich sestřih naleznete v tomto videu.

– Tereza Sladkovská (budoucí Urzová xD), dlouholetá editorka a autorka Ludwig von Mises Institutu, členka Students for Liberty

title_en: Anarcho-Capitalism on the Front Line: The Road to Anarcho-Capitalism
text_en:
Radio Free Transmitter (Slobodný vysielač) deals, among other things, with anarcho-capitalism in the program In the first line; they approached me to be their regular guest, which I happily accepted.
In this part, we focused on the transition to an anarcho-capitalist society from today's state-run society. How to achieve something like this? How long can such a transformation take?

– Urza (www.urza.cz); author of Anarchocapitalism; creator of Freeport; co-founder and head of the Ludwig von Mises Institute; member of the Freedom of Learning board

text_cs:
Ačkoliv je v LGBTQ komunitě mnoho etatistů, kteří se snaží svou agendu tlačit skrze státní moc, v některých věcech mají pravdu. My nesouhlasíme s násilím skrze stát a omezování svobody projevu, neboť jsme přesvědčeni, že tou správnou cestou je osvěta.

– Tereza Sladkovská (budoucí Urzová xD), dlouholetá editorka a autorka Ludwig von Mises Institutu, členka Students for Liberty

One planned lecture at the (de)Centrála club became a regular cycle (every first Wednesday of the month) due to great interest; the latter to some extent follows the cycle Anarchocapitalismus in Parallel Polis, although the format changes a little. I would like to shorten my talk, increase the space for discussion and deformalize everything a bit; moreover, I probably won't be the only one lecturing.
The topic of the lecture and discussion will be intellectual property, which loosely follows the principle of non-aggression, which we talked about last time. How does intellectual property relate to property rights? And how might its enforcement differ today and in a stateless society? The lecture will require full attention, as the issue of intellectual property in anarcho-capitalism is often misinterpreted.
Presentation: https://prednasky.urza.cz/decentrala/

– Urza (www.urza.cz); author of Anarchocapitalism; creator of Freeport; co-founder and head of the Ludwig von Mises Institute; member of the Freedom of Learning board

text_cs:
Během přednášky na gymnáziu v Holicích jsem zmínil, že evoluční teorie není dokázaná; reakce byly silné a často až šokované.
V online i osobní diskusi na toto téma s řadou lidí jsem seznal, že by bylo dobré natočit video, kde vysvětlím, co to vlastně znamená vědecký důkaz a jaký je rozdíl mezi ním a pouhým experimentem nevyvracejícím teorii.

– Urza (www.urza.cz)
title_en: Interview for Svobodné universum: Forward to the past
text_en:
The lovely Martina Kociánová did this great interview with me, in which she proved to be a very capable presenter. With her kind permission, I am then publishing the recording on the Freeport Channel. You can find all parts of the interview (here they are combined into one) here:
https://www.kupredudominulosti.cz/host/urza/

– Urza (www.urza.cz); author of Anarchocapitalism; creator of Freeport; co-founder and head of the Ludwig von Mises Institute; member of the Freedom of Learning board

text_cs:
Byli jsme na dovolené, létali na padaglidech, zasnoubili se (ve vzduchu); máme úžasný život a chceme jej prožít spolu. I v tomto spíše osobním videu naleznete pár anarchokapitalistických myšlenek, ačkoliv tentokrát výjimečně nejsou hlavním tématem.

– Tereza Sladkovská (budoucí Urzová xD), dlouholetá editorka a autorka Ludwig von Mises Institutu, členka Students for Liberty
– Urza (www.urza.cz), tvůrce STOK SVOBODNÉHO PŘÍSTAVU, spoluzakladatel Ludwig von Mises Institutu, člen Svobody učení
text_en:
Petr Smidrkal, one of the generous funders of the Free Port, invited me to a lecture in his hometown Rakovník; this time I tried to introduce people to anarcho-capitalism in a slightly different way than before. And I think it was successful; after all, judge for yourself!

– Urza (www.urza.cz); author of Anarchocapitalism; creator of Freeport; co-founder and head of the Ludwig von Mises Institute; member of the Freedom of Learning board

text_cs:
Naši poslanci po dlouhé době výjimečně udělali něco, za co jsme je dokonce pochválili; na druhou stranu předseda Zelených Matěj Stropnický to nepřekvapivě vidí jinak. A protože nezareagoval na pozvání do diskuse, jeho výrok jsme okomentovali ve videu.

– Tereza Sladkovská (budoucí Urzová xD), dlouholetá editorka a autorka Ludwig von Mises Institutu, členka Students for Liberty
– Urza (www.urza.cz), tvůrce STOK SVOBODNÉHO PŘÍSTAVU, spoluzakladatel Ludwig von Mises Institutu, člen Svobody učení
title_en: Kinolab Film Festival: Folk Art in Cyberspace
text_en:
Kinolab.cz invited me to the panel discussion "Folk art in cyberspace"; the central theme was intellectual property. In the debate, I brought anarcho-capitalist views between the three lawyers, which was quite unconventional; the discussion was not confrontational, but I found it very interesting (especially thanks to my opponents).

– Urza (www.urza.cz); author of Anarchocapitalism; creator of Freeport; co-founder and head of the Ludwig von Mises Institute; member of the Freedom of Learning board

text_cs:
Studenti gymnázia v Holicích mě pozvali na den osobností, abych jim přednášel o anarchokapitalismu, svobodě (i Svobodě) učení, vzdělávání a státu; rád jsem přijal a přijel, ačkoliv termín kolidoval s pozváním na stejnou akci jiného gymnázia.
Na přednášku dorazili nejen studenti a učitelé, ale k mému překvapení i někteří rodiče; nakonec se rozproudila zajímavá debata, s jejímž výsledkem jsem určitě spokojen, ale to už posuďte sami.
Jedná se bohužel jen o audiozáznam nahrávaný do telefonu, obraz není a ani kvalita zvuku neumožňuje zrovna nejluxusnější poslech, za což se omlouvám; považuji jej však za poslouchatelný.
– Urza (www.urza.cz)
text_en:
E15 (info.cz) invited me to their program Štrunc! They were kind enough to allow me to publish the recording of the interview on the Freeport Channel, for which I thank them here. Above all, however, anarcho-capitalism is becoming known to the wider public; for that, thank you to everyone who participates or supports us.
#makeAncapMainstream

– Urza (www.urza.cz); author of Anarchocapitalism; creator of Freeport; co-founder and head of the Ludwig von Mises Institute; member of the Freedom of Learning board

text_cs:
Paralelní Polis uspořádala diskusi na téma „Sdílená ekonomika“ – fenomén dnešní doby, modla a strašák. Vyhledávané služby, které svou úspěšností u uživatelů poráží zaběhnuté firmy a děsí stát. 
Urza byl pozván jako host, Tereza vybrala z diskuse zajímavé momenty a přidala svůj komentář.

– Tereza Sladkovská (budoucí Urzová xD), dlouholetá editorka a autorka Ludwig von Mises Institutu, členka Students for Liberty
– Urza (www.urza.cz), tvůrce STOK SVOBODNÉHO PŘÍSTAVU, spoluzakladatel Ludwig von Mises Institutu, člen Svobody učení
title_en: Jana Kozlová and Urza on the state, laws and education
text_en:
Nonviolent communication lecturer Jana Kozlova and I differed on the law prohibiting physical punishment for children, which was presented in France; although none of us physically punishes children, neither of us likes it, but I am convinced that the state should not interfere in such a thing at all.

– Urza (www.urza.cz); author of Anarchocapitalism; creator of Freeport; co-founder and head of the Ludwig von Mises Institute; member of the Freedom of Learning board

text_cs:
Inovace mohou probíhat – a již po tisíciletí probíhají – na základě dobrovolnosti vynalézavých a podnikavých lidí; takový stav je více než žádoucí a díky němu naše společnost stále vzkvétá. Krom toho tu máme bohužel nenechavý, rozežraný a rozpínavý stát, jenž bere lidem prostředky proti jejich vůli pod hrozbou použití násilí vůči nim; i v důsledku jeho zásahů vznikají různé inovace, nicméně za jakou cenu?
Přednáší Urza (www.urza.cz).
text_en:
After two years, I was invited again to the Budějovická Gymnasium; but I did not enter the same river a second time. Whereas anarcho-capitalism was unknown there last time, this time the awareness was much deeper; and there were even sympathizers and even readers of my book among the students. #makeAncapMainstream

– Urza (www.urza.cz); author of Anarchocapitalism; creator of Freeport; co-founder and head of the Ludwig von Mises Institute; member of the Freedom of Learning board

text_cs:
Paralelní Polis uspořádala diskusi na téma „Protikuřácký zákon“; má vláda „chránit naše zdraví“, nebo by nikdo neměl být násilím nucen uzpůsobovat pravidla ve svém podniku rozkazům mocných?
Urza byl pozván jako host, Tereza vybrala z diskuse zajímavé momenty a přidala svůj komentář.

– Tereza Sladkovská (budoucí Urzová xD), dlouholetá editorka a autorka Ludwig von Mises Institutu, členka Students for Liberty

title_en: Students for Liberty: Is the State Legitimate? Backa versus Urza
text_en:
Students for Liberty: How are taxes different from protection money? Is it legitimate for the state to force citizens to do something they have not consented to? We will seek answers to these and other questions in the context of the debate between the propagator of anarcho-capitalism Urza and the lawyer Jakub Backa as part of the Liberty Evening.

– Urza (www.urza.cz); author of Anarchocapitalism; creator of Freeport; co-founder and head of the Ludwig von Mises Institute; member of the Freedom of Learning board

title_cs: Anarchokapitalismus, díl jedenáctý: Kdo by stavěl silnice?
text_cs:
„Kdybychom neměli stát, kdo by stavěl silnice?“ Tak zní nejčastější otázka v libertariánských vtipech a jedna z prvních reakcí etatistů na zmínku o bezstátní společnosti; právě tuto otázku se chystám na přednášce zodpovědět. A nejen to! Povídat si budeme i o pravidlech silničního provozu; lišily by se tyto cestu od cesty, kdyby měla každá pozemní komunikace svého soukromého vlastníka? Po přednášce bude jako vždy (snad bouřlivá) diskuse; těším se na vás, zejména pokud se mnou nesouhlasíte!
Přednáší Urza (www.urza.cz).

One planned lecture at the (de)Centrála club became a regular cycle (every first Wednesday of the month) due to great interest; the latter to some extent follows the cycle Anarchocapitalismus in Parallel Polis, although the format changes a little. I would like to shorten my talk, increase the space for discussion and deformalize everything a bit; moreover, I probably won't be the only one lecturing.
The topic of the lecture and discussion will be the increasingly asked and mentioned non-aggression principle (NAP). We will explain in detail what it actually is, what it is good for, but also mainly what it is definitely not good for; we will also touch on topics such as psychological violence or animal rights, about which there are heated discussions in connection with the NAP.
Presentation: https://prednasky.urza.cz/decentrala/

– Urza (www.urza.cz); author of Anarchocapitalism; creator of Freeport; co-founder and head of the Ludwig von Mises Institute; member of the Freedom of Learning board

title_cs: Anarchokapitalismus, díl desátý: Veřejný prostor a svoboda slova
text_cs:
Na desáté přednášce z cyklu Anarchokapitalismus se budeme věnovat veřejným prostranstvím a místům „pro všechny“; jak by mohly takové prostory existovat v bezstátní společnosti založené na respektu k vlastnickým právům? Kdo by je spravoval, proč a za co? Zanikly by ve městech všechny parky? Žili bychom v betonových džunglích bez kousku zeleně? Krom toho si budeme povídat o svobodě slova; jak ta s tématem souvisí? Ukážeme si, že velice těsně. Po přednášce bude jako vždy následovat diskuse; doufám, že mi budete oponovat!
Přednáší Urza (www.urza.cz).
Prezentace: https://prednasky.urza.cz/ankup/
text_en:
The lecture on anarcho-capitalism was also requested by the Pirate Party; although I am not exactly a fan of them, I believe that it is always good to have a dialogue, so I gladly accepted. In the end, Terezka also lectured with me; you can watch its premiere in this recording.

– Tereza Urzová; creator of Freeport; head of the Ludwig von Mises Institute; publisher of the book Anarchocapitalismus; member of Students for Liberty
– Urza (www.urza.cz); author of Anarchocapitalism; creator of Freeport; co-founder and head of the Ludwig von Mises Institute; member of the Freedom of Learning board

text_cs:
Dnes se zamýšlíme nad volbou francouzského prezidenta (a rozhodně Francouzům nezávidíme ten výběr), poslední volbou českého prezidenta a hlavně vůbec nad tím, k čemu je vůbec dobré (kdekoliv) prezidenta mít…

– Tereza Sladkovská (budoucí Urzová xD), dlouholetá editorka a autorka Ludwig von Mises Institutu, členka Students for Liberty
– Urza (www.urza.cz), tvůrce STOK SVOBODNÉHO PŘÍSTAVU, spoluzakladatel Ludwig von Mises Institutu, člen Svobody učení
text_en:
Parlamentní Listy and TV Praha invited me to the program Na ostří nože; my opponent in the duel was Lukáš Jelínek and the topic was democracy. You can watch the full uncut version of the entire debate here; you saw less than half in the Parliamentary Papers.

– Urza (www.urza.cz); author of Anarchocapitalism; creator of Freeport; co-founder and head of the Ludwig von Mises Institute; member of the Freedom of Learning board

text_cs:
Paralelní Polis uspořádala diskusi na téma „Stát versus práce“; má vláda chránit české pracovníky před levnou pracovní silou z východu?
Urza byl pozván jako host, Tereza vybrala z diskuse zajímavé momenty a přidala svůj komentář.

– Tereza Sladkovská (budoucí Urzová xD), dlouholetá editorka a autorka Ludwig von Mises Institutu, členka Students for Liberty
– Urza (www.urza.cz), tvůrce STOK SVOBODNÉHO PŘÍSTAVU, spoluzakladatel Ludwig von Mises Institutu, člen Svobody učení
text_en:
HAD KLUB is a student club in Liberec, where I was invited to discuss anarcho-capitalism. There was a great atmosphere in the place and I have to say that some of the best questions ever were asked; it's rare that there are so many people sitting in the audience with such a desire to learn something.

– Urza (www.urza.cz); author of Anarchocapitalism; creator of Freeport; co-founder and head of the Ludwig von Mises Institute; member of the Freedom of Learning board

text_cs:
Tématem deváté přednášky z cyklu Anarchokapitalismus budou zbraně a jejich regulace; povíme si o tom, k čemu vede odzbrojování společnosti a v čem se především liší společenství lidí se zbraněmi a bez nich. Ohlédneme se i do historie a zaměříme se na dobu a místo, kdy a kde byly zbraně prakticky neregulované; jaké to mělo důsledky? Přednášku jako vždy zakončí diskuse, ve které se budete moci na cokoliv zeptat a ideálně mi i oponovat.
Přednáší Urza (www.urza.cz).
Prezentace: https://prednasky.urza.cz/ankup/
text_en:
Cafebar Dark Velvet organized an anarchist evening; in addition to the author's reading, debates and a bit of poetry, my short lecture with a subsequent debate was also on the program. The recording is only of this part of the evening; however, it was certainly not the last event of this type in Dark Velvet, next time you can come too!

– Urza (www.urza.cz); author of Anarchocapitalism; creator of Freeport; co-founder and head of the Ludwig von Mises Institute; member of the Freedom of Learning board

text_cs:
Protože v KANÁLU SVOBODNÉHO PŘÍSTAVU většinou dštíme oheň a síru na stát, tentokrát jsme se rozhodli být pozitivní, milí a podělit se s vámi, vážení diváci, o trochu štěstí z krásného jarního dne; pojeďte se s námi projet xD

– Tereza Sladkovská (budoucí Urzová xD), dlouholetá editorka a autorka Ludwig von Mises Institutu, členka Students for Liberty
– Urza (www.urza.cz), tvůrce STOK SVOBODNÉHO PŘÍSTAVU, spoluzakladatel Ludwig von Mises Institutu, člen Svobody učení
text_en:
It was a great honor for me to speak at the Svobodome, where we organized an autumn stay with the Freedom of Learning. The speech and the subsequent debate naturally concerned primarily freedom in education, but subsequently also anarcho-capitalism as a whole and the possibilities of how far we can go with freedom in individual branches of human activity; does it make sense to want freedom for yourself, but at the same time deny it to others?

– Urza (www.urza.cz); author of Anarchocapitalism; creator of Freeport; co-founder and head of the Ludwig von Mises Institute; member of the Freedom of Learning board

text_cs:
Na osmé přednášce z cyklu Anarchokapitalismus si budeme povídat a diskutovat o drogách; jednak se budeme bavit o drogách samotných, ale především o vztahu státu k nim a naší svobodě nakládat s vlastním tělem dle svého uvážení. Probírat budeme také válku proti drogám, která zuří již dlouhá desetiletí; co nás vlastně stála a jaké má výsledky? Po přednášce bude již tradičně následovat diskuse, ve které se s radostí pokusím zodpovědět všechny otázky, které mi položíte.
Přednáší Urza (www.urza.cz).

title_en: Urza versus Antonín Dolák at Stigura about monopolies
text_en:
In the last debate with Stigur, we did not have time to discuss monopolies and agreed to do a sequel; Stigur (https://www.twitch.tv/stigur_cz) invited my critic Antonín Dolák (https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCetB9vSWnvoUV3s_OOv0BHA?view_as=subscriber) to it and he himself decided on the role of moderator.

– Urza (www.urza.cz); author of Anarchocapitalism; creator of Freeport; co-founder and head of the Ludwig von Mises Institute; member of the Freedom of Learning board

text_cs:
Kdo je Marek Novák? Náš nejvytrvalejší a nejproslulejší troll.
Chcete znát jeho identitu? Sledujte toto video!

– Tereza Sladkovská (budoucí Urzová xD), dlouholetá editorka a autorka Ludwig von Mises Institutu, členka Students for Liberty

title_en: Anarcho-Capitalism on the Front Line: Law Enforcement
text_en:
Radio Free Transmitter (Slobodný vysielač) deals, among other things, with anarcho-capitalism in the program In the first line; they approached me to be their regular guest, which I happily accepted.
In this piece, we tackled one of the most difficult topics, namely free market law enforcement; we dealt with what happens if someone damages someone else and refuses to take any responsibility for it.

– Urza (www.urza.cz); author of Anarchocapitalism; creator of Freeport; co-founder and head of the Ludwig von Mises Institute; member of the Freedom of Learning board

text_cs:
17. až 19. března probíhal v Praze LibertyCon, kterého jsme se zúčastnili a přinášíme vám z něj krátký sestřih videí, jež jsme tam natočili; celá akce byla naprosto fenomenálně boží.
Snad se tam příští rok potkáme i s vámi!

– Tereza Sladkovská (budoucí Urzová xD), dlouholetá editorka a autorka Ludwig von Mises Institutu, členka Students for Liberty
– Urza (www.urza.cz), tvůrce STOK SVOBODNÉHO PŘÍSTAVU, spoluzakladatel Ludwig von Mises Institutu, člen Svobody učení
text_en:
I was approached by Petr Höhn with his Urban XP project, where he conducts interesting interviews with various people; I was very happy to answer his questions about anarcho-capitalism. He was kind enough to allow me to upload the result to the Freeport Channel.

– Urza (www.urza.cz); author of Anarchocapitalism; creator of Freeport; co-founder and head of the Ludwig von Mises Institute; member of the Freedom of Learning board

text_cs:
Presentation of Freedom to Learn (Svoboda učení) at LibertyCon 2017.
The government is indoctrinating our kids with propaganda of statism and evil; the solution is the separation of state and education!

Presenting: Urza (www.urza.cz) and Zdeňka Staňková of Svoboda učení (www.svobodauceni.cz).
title_en: Synergeticum: The Different Faces of Anarchy III
text_en:
The collectivist anarchist Tibor Moravčík invited me to his radio show; and I find it extremely interesting to discuss anarchy from two completely opposite perspectives and approaches. Anarcho-capitalists use logic, collectivist anarchists more emotion; before i would have said logic is just better, today i just don't know. I am an anarcho-capitalist, but I respect anarchists of other schools.

– Urza (www.urza.cz); author of Anarchocapitalism; creator of Freeport; co-founder and head of the Ludwig von Mises Institute; member of the Freedom of Learning board

text_cs:
Tuto přednášku považuji za nejdůležitější z celého cyklu o Anarchokapitalismu; povídat si budeme o státním vzdělávacím systému coby mocném nástroji využívanému k masivnímu šíření státní propagandy. Budeme rozkrývat kořeny i dopady toho, jak současné školství funguje. text_cs:
V roce 2009 dala EU Intelu antimonopolní pokutu ve výši $1,1 miliardy za „conditional rebates“ (sleva pro ty, kdo nakupují v podstatě jen u něj) a „naked restrictions“ (platby těm, kdo nenakupují u konkurence); Intel se s EU soudil a v roce 2022 vyhrál, protože se u „conditional rebates“ EU nepodařilo prokázat konkrétní dopad na konkurenci (a v pokutě nebylo určeno, která část je za „conditional rebates“ a která za „naked restrictions“). V roce 2023 EU prokázala dopady „naked restrictions“, za které uložila Intelu pokutu $386 milionů; jenže Intel zažaloval EU o ušlé úroky z neoprávněné pokuty, což za těch 15 let vyšplhalo na $536. Celý soudní spor tedy stál daňové poplatníky $150 milionů – nepočítáme-li výdaje na orgány Evropské unie, které rozhodnutí zpackaly a následně dlouhá léta řešily.

Ten příběh si (krom našich peněz) zaslouží i Hitlerův komentář s titulky, nemyslíte?

title_en: Synergeticum: The Different Faces of Anarchy I
text_en:
The collectivist anarchist Tibor Moravčík invited me to his radio show; and I find it extremely interesting to discuss anarchy from two completely opposite perspectives and approaches. Anarcho-capitalists use logic, collectivist anarchists more emotion; before i would have said logic is just better, today i just don't know. I am an anarcho-capitalist, but I respect anarchists of other schools.

title_en: Anarcho-capitalism in the Brno Impact Hub
text_en:
Svobodní invited me to give a lecture at the Impact Hub in Brno about the very foundations of anarcho-capitalism. Although I did not expect that many people would come, because libertarian lectures are not so popular in Moravia, they filled the whole large hall, about a hundred of them came; and many of them didn't know ankap at all, they came to me after the lecture and said that they are becoming interested because it makes sense to them, which is the best appreciation of my work.

– Urza (www.urza.cz); author of Anarchocapitalism; creator of Freeport; co-founder and head of the Ludwig von Mises Institute; member of the Freedom of Learning board

One planned lecture at the (de)Centrála club became a regular cycle (every first Wednesday of the month) due to great interest; the latter to some extent follows the cycle Anarchocapitalismus in Parallel Polis, although the format changes a little. I would like to shorten my talk, increase the space for discussion and deformalize everything a bit; moreover, I probably won't be the only one lecturing.
The topic of both the lecture and the discussion will be something that, in connection with the growing popularity of anarcho-capitalism, is increasingly coming under fire, namely monopolization in the free market. Will monopolies and cartel agreements arise without state supervision and antitrust authorities? How does the Austrian school of economics view monopoly? What about mainstream economics? Without a state, do we have anything to fear? If you are interested in answers - not only to these questions - do not hesitate to come!
Presentation: https://prednasky.urza.cz/decentrala/

title_en: SKAV: What values does the school teach?
text_en:
As many of you probably know, as part of my anarcho-capitalist and libertarian activities, I focus primarily on education. As a member of Freedom of Learning, I represent the Freedom of Learning Association in SKAV (Permanent Conference of Associations in Education). SKAV organizes Round Tables (panel discussions), of which I found this one absolutely essential, so I am making its recording available. Please note that this is far more an educational and professional debate than a libertarian one, so it's different than what you're used to.

title_en: Anarcho-Capitalism, Part Nineteen: In the Broader Context...
text_en:
How to go from a huge omnivorous state to anarcho-capitalism? And where does the road definitely not lead? We will also talk about this at the last regular lecture of this cycle. Many of you have rightly noted that most of the lectures were "one-of-a-kind" in the sense of applying the same principle to various branches of human endeavor. I would like to clarify and formulate this principle in general terms; especially for those who didn't notice it. And finally, we will place anarcho-capitalism in some context of the other anarchist schools, of which there are many and about which you will certainly hear a lot more.
Lectures by Urza (www.urza.cz).
Presentation: https://prednasky.urza.cz/ankup/

title_cs: Studio Svobodného přístavu: Pragmatismus v(ersus) idealismu(s)
text_cs:
https://www.startovac.cz/projekty/anarchoagorismus
https://kniha.urza.cz/
Poslední dobou často (bohužel i z řad libertariánů) slýchám, že s ohledem (zejména) na současnou (geo)politickou situaci „není čas na anarchismus“, protože idealismus je třeba nahradit pragmatismem; já si však nemyslím, že to jde proti sobě – anarchismus považuji za zcela pragmatický přístup.
Během livestreamu budeme zároveň vybírat peníze na knihu; už proto, že v ní tohle téma hodně rezonuje.

– Urza (www.urza.cz); autor knihy Anarchokapitalismus; tvůrce Svobodného přístavu; spoluzakladatel a hlava Institutu Ludwiga von Misese; člen předsednictva Svobody učení; dospělák v Ježku bez klece
text_en:
As difficult as the free market provision of justice and internal security is, defense against an external enemy and, by extension, international relations represent by far the greatest challenge for a stateless anarcho-capitalist society. Can free people without a state defend themselves against aggressive conquerors? And if not, what will happen in the conquered territory? How does the control of a conquered anarchist territory differ from the control of a conquered state? Can the common survive without the state? Minarchists do not believe this; anarcho-capitalists do. Don't miss a lecture with a discussion on this interesting topic.
Lectures by Urza (www.urza.cz).
Presentation: https://prednasky.urza.cz/ankup/

Seberozvoj mnedle úzce souvisí s anarchismem – (nejen) v knize Anarchoagorismus vysvětluji proč; s Jíťou se seberozvoji věnujeme, tak o něm chceme mluvit.
Rádi bychom se věnovali praktickému příkladu – mé ztrátě autenticity a vnitřní motivace během kampaně na knihu; je to pro mě náročné, ale chci o tom mluvit.

– Urza (www.urza.cz); autor knihy Anarchokapitalismus; tvůrce Svobodného přístavu; spoluzakladatel a hlava Institutu Ludwiga von Misese; člen předsednictva Svobody učení; dospělák v Ježku bez klece
text_en:
If the lecture on the judiciary was controversial, it is doubly so for law enforcement. While last time we only dealt with disputes in which both parties more or less cooperate, this time we will talk about cases of criminals and desperadoes who violate property rights and actively try to avoid the administration of justice. How will the free market deal with them? Isn't the state really needed here? This lecture is one of the three most "advanced" of the series and is a bone of contention between the anarcho-capitalists and the minarchists; so don't miss it.
Lectures by Urza (www.urza.cz).

How could a free market without states ensure a functioning judiciary? Who would appoint a judge? And would it be possible to appeal against the judgment? Is there any way to prevent the courts from favoring rich and wealthy clients? I will try to answer these - and many other - questions during the lecture; but first of all we get to the most interesting part: What would the courts decide if there was no central authority with a monopoly on legislation? This lecture is one of the three most "advanced" of the series and is a bone of contention between the anarcho-capitalists and the minarchists; so don't miss it.

Na rozdíl od ostatních běžných livestreamů nebudeme řešit žádné jedno konkrétní téma, takže můžeme probírat cokoliv, co si budete přát; a jako v případě předchozích streamaratonů můžeme tematicky občas i trochu (víc) vybočovat mimo libertarianismus.

text_en:
When the word "free market health care" is mentioned, most people immediately think of exorbitant amounts of money for medical procedures that the common mortal simply cannot afford to pay, leaving him with no choice but to live in sickness; or even die. Without the government, how could we afford to pay for medical care? Who would supervise the quality? How to overcome the enormous information asymmetry between doctor and patient in the market? Isn't free market healthcare an antisocial and horrible system through which the powerful can squeeze the powerless and sick? You will learn the answers to these and many other questions when you come to the lecture; and you can ask your own questions in the subsequent discussion.

title_en: HCPP17: Liberate education from the state!
text_en:
Compulsory school attendance is not only immoral, but it also represents the initial reason for our economic lack of freedom; State education costs money, also it's a source of state propaganda and statist indoctrination. This is the main cause of the conviction of people that the free market fails in so many areas, so we need the state authority to replace it. Why don't they teach us anything about the impossibility of economic calculation in the central planning? How easily can the authority of a teacher be replaced by the state authorities? And how can we keep the freedom when we spend the most important years of our lives in the jail?
Sorry for my horrible English; it is not so good in general and moreover I felt physically quite bad this time.

Presenting: Zdeňka Staňková and Urza (www.urza.cz) of Freedom of Learning (www.svobodauceni.cz).

title_en: Anarcho-Capitalism, Part Eleven: Who Would Build the Roads?
text_en:
"If we had no state, who would build the roads?" So goes the most common question in libertarian jokes and one of the first reactions of statists to the mention of a stateless society; I am going to answer this very question at the lecture. And not only that! We will also talk about road traffic rules; would these differ from road to road if each road had its own private owner? After the lecture, as always, there will be a (perhaps heated) discussion; I look forward to hearing from you, especially if you disagree with me!
